newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares soar 5.8 pct in strong volume.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares soar 5.8 pct in strong volume.

text.p: Turkish shares rallied in strong activity led by utilities and state-run firms on Monday amid positive sentiment after political concerns died down last week, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,586, up 87 points, or 5.8 percent from Friday, following last week's 3.88 percent gain caused by positive political developments.
Trade volume further jumped to 43.9 trillion lira from Friday's 32 trillion.

Brokers said sentiment was further buoyed by positive news concerning ties with the European Union, following a weekend meeting of the EU foreign ministers who reassured Turkey that it could one day qualify for membership.
They said the release of all 1996 financial results which had a Friday deadline also fuelled selective buys in firms which sharply increased their 1996 profits.
"The market will probably maintain its uptrend this week, but steep rises such as today's are unlikely," said Ali Ilgaz from Global securities.

Of the 238 shares traded, rises outdid falls sharply by 177 to 35 and 26 finished stable. The IMKB Industrial gained 3.89 percent to 1,601, the IMKB Services surged 8.54 percent to 1,487 and the IMKB Financial jumped 6.22 percent to 1,656.

The most heavily traded shares were utilities Cukurova Elektrik, up 27,500 lira at 217,500, Aktas Elektrik, up 15,000 lira at 190,000 and state oil refiner Tupras, up 7,000 lira at 70,000. They made up 21.3 percent of the total turnover.
